definitions.candidateEntry: An accepted Animalia species entry in the frozen global IUCN CR/EN/VU pool with verified marine evidence from WoRMS under the project's name checks.
definitions.tradeIdentified: At least one uniquely attributed positive-quantity original record for this candidate in the frozen 2015–2024 Appendix I–III extract, on either reporting side.
definitions.annualCoverage: Number of distinct IUCN candidate taxon IDs with at least one identified core record in the year, with risk category held fixed to IUCN 2026-1.
definitions.annualRecordsCount: Count of original source line items per year for a candidate. Not transactions, animals or a sum of quantities.
definitions.classMatrix: Counts grouped by the candidate's frozen IUCN class, not by potentially differing CITES classification fields.
definitions.publicationYear: IUCN publication/reference year supplied in the frozen checklist, not an inferred assessment date.

limitations: This is the project's verified candidate list, not a complete census of all threatened marine species worldwide.
The list contains 1,608 IUCN candidate entries, corresponding to 1,601 accepted WoRMS taxon IDs. They are not interchangeable totals.
Twelve candidate entries belong to unresolved many-to-one taxonomic joins. Trade records are not assigned to them automatically.
IUCN 2026-1 categories define the groups throughout this story; they do not reconstruct each species' status in each historical trade year.
Identified trade coverage uses only CITES Appendix I, II or III records in 2015–2024 from the frozen full database 2026.1.
No identified record does not mean no trade, no exploitation, or no threat. CITES coverage and reporting can differ among taxa and years.
Other candidate entries includes both eligible entries without an identified core record and unresolved taxonomic joins.
A candidate can occur in more than one year. Summing annual coverage cells does not give the number of distinct candidates across the decade.
Original line-item counts are not shipments, independent transactions, quantities of animals, or population estimates.
Importer and exporter reports can describe the same trade. Their quantities are not added here; this story counts identified candidate entries.
A trade record does not establish that trade caused a species' risk category or that a transaction was illegal.
Reported product terms are not a verified map of body parts or consumer uses. Anomalous terms are retained as source records rather than treated as biological facts.
This frozen full-database snapshot can differ from the preceding single-species page's live comparative-tabulation extract. Quantities and row counts must not be mixed between snapshots.
